prompt: Analyse the impact of globalisation on economic growth and inequality in developing economies.
stmt_text: Analyse the impact of globalisation on economic growth and inequality in developing economies.
sol_text:
Model answer:
Globalisation gives developing economies access to larger markets, FDI, technology and finance.
Countries that opened up (e.g. China, Vietnam) had rapid export-led growth, lifting hundreds of millions out of poverty.
However, the gains are unequal: skilled workers, urban areas and owners of capital benefit most, so inequality within countries has often risen.
Some countries, especially in Sub-Saharan Africa, remain reliant on commodity exports and are exposed to price swings and capital outflows.
Overall, globalisation has raised growth and reduced global poverty, but has widened inequality within many developing economies unless governments invest in education and safety nets.

prompt: Analyse the effects of reducing protection on the Australian economy.

prompt: Explain how an increase in the cash rate affects aggregate demand and inflation.
stmt_text: Explain how an increase in the cash rate affects aggregate demand and inflation.
sol_text:
Model answer:
The RBA raises the cash rate target; banks pass this on through higher lending and deposit rates.
Higher mortgage repayments cut household disposable income and borrowing becomes dearer, so consumption and investment fall; saving is more attractive.
Higher rates also tend to appreciate the AUD, reducing net exports.
Lower aggregate demand reduces pressure on prices and wages, so inflation falls back toward the 2–3% target after a lag.

Higher mortgage repayments cut household disposable income and borrowing becomes dearer, so consumption and investment fall; saving is more attractive.

Higher rates also tend to appreciate the AUD, reducing net exports.

Lower aggregate demand reduces pressure on prices and wages, so inflation falls back toward the 2–3% target after a lag.
